summary.ground_truth: Hand-written by the author. SQL cases are graded against a gold query run on the frozen ops_eval database at eval time; policy cases against the sections the author identified in data/policies; refusals and proposals against the status the loop records; the tenant case against the other restaurant's figure, which must not appear. Every case also checks that each query the guard let through was pinned to the asking restaurant.

case.question: How many catering orders did we do in September?
case.note: A catering order is one with an item from the Catering category on the menu. Nothing on the order itself says catering: no channel, no label, no discount. Three ad hoc asks on 1 November, about October, all searched the order's labels, found nothing, and said the data cannot identify catering orders. The first version asked about October, the month in progress on the frozen clock, and the agent rightly stopped at the 24th while the gold did not.
case.gold_sql:
-- sql-11: How many catering orders did we do in September?

SELECT count(DISTINCT o.id)
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN items i ON i.id = oi.item_id
JOIN categories c ON c.id = i.category_id
WHERE o.state = 'completed'
  AND c.name = 'Catering'
  AND o.created_at >= timestamp '2026-09-01' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago'
  AND o.created_at <  timestamp '2026-10-01' AT TIME ZONE 'America/Chicago'

trace.question: How many catering orders did we do in September?
trace.answer:
We did 22 catering orders in September 2026. I counted completed orders that included at least one item from the Catering category, using local time for the month boundaries. Those orders had combined gross sales of $3,634.62. The gross figure covers the whole order, so it includes any non-catering items on the same ticket.

The policies don't define "catering" beyond the menu category, so I used the category. [House Policy §6, Catering] covers catering notice, deposits and cancellations, but it doesn't change the count.

detail.sql: select c.name cat, i.name, i.id from categories c left join items i on i.category_id=c.id where c.name ilike '%cater%' or i.name ilike '%cater%'

SELECT c.name AS cat, i.name, i.id FROM (SELECT * FROM categories WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS c LEFT JOIN (SELECT * FROM items WHERE merchant_id = 1) AS i ON i.category_id = c.id WHERE c.name ILIKE '%cater%' OR i.name ILIKE '%cater%' LIMIT 500
